France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/fires-heat-floods-extreme-weather-2026</link>
      <description><p>People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe</p><p>After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.</p><p>As <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/cop31">Cop31</a> continues and scientists warn that <a href="https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261027231200.htm">climate breakdown may be accelerating</a>, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/fires-heat-floods-extreme-weather-2026">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather</link>
      <description><p>Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week </p><p>Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.</p><p>After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack which Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine </p><p>Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone maker in the Baltic state over the weekend, which authorities said was ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service.</p><p>On Saturday morning, eight people were detained during an attempted attack on Threod Systems, a defence company that manufactures long-range attack and reconnaissance drones.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/czechia-protest-prague-media-freedom</link>
      <description><p>Estimated 350,000 people rally against plan to scrap licence fees and fund broadcasters from state budget</p><p>Hundreds of thousands of Czechs have rallied in Prague to protest against a perceived government attempt to stifle media freedom.</p><p>The gathering on Sunday to save the mandatory licence fees that fund Czechia’s public broadcasters drew more than 350,000 people, making it one of the biggest in the country’s history, organisers said.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/czechia-protest-prague-media-freedom">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>How a US extradition bid over Hamas allegations put a wealthy activist before a Spanish court</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/activist-extradition-gaza-hamas-spanish-court</link>
      <description><p>James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas</p><p>A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.</p><p>Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/07/trump-administration-altered-translation-request-extradite-fergie-chambers">reported on</a> – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/activist-extradition-gaza-hamas-spanish-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2026/nov/14/eurotunnel-drive-in-fingerprint-trial-folkestone-calais-border</link>
      <description><p>Eurotunnel owner Getlink wants to replicate ‘airport experience’ at Folkestone and Calais, without making people get out of cars</p><p>Airport-style passport and fingerprinting controls are to be introduced at Eurotunnel in an attempt to prevent “short-term and long-term chaos” in Folkestone and Calais.</p><p>In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has agreed to a new system in which an “eagle eye” camera system, already used in Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging, will be used at the border between the UK and France.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2026/nov/14/eurotunnel-drive-in-fingerprint-trial-folkestone-calais-border">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:56:22 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>
Five families of Harkis – Algerians who fought for the French during Algeria's war of independence – have filed a legal complaint seeking answers over children who died in the 1960s in a former Harki camp in the south of France, and whose remains have since disappeared.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cb9c44a8-dded-11f1-9b62-d30335cd8455</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:07:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Women in France report painful periods after exposure to tear gas at protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-women-in-france-report-painful-periods-after-exposure-to-tear-gas-at-protests</link><description>
Thousands of women in France have reported unusually painful periods, heavy bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after being exposed to tear gas during the country's recent protests, prompting calls for an investigation into its possible effects on reproductive health.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>How France's student protests grew into a broader movement amid police violence</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-how-france-s-student-protests-grew-into-a-broader-movement-amid-police-violence</link><description>
What began in September as a student protest over deteriorating school conditions has over recent weeks grown into a broader social movement across France. The violent police response, notably against young protesters, has helped galvanise support, drawing in university students, trade unions and the wider public.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5254f58-dea5-11f1-81d0-4703a0e08d35</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:11:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters</source><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fifth wave of French protests to focus on child protection and police laws</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-fifth-wave-of-french-protests-to-focus-on-child-protection-and-police-laws</link><description>
France faces more rallies on Saturday with demonstrators venting frustrations ranging from inflation, to child protection measures and opposition to a new police bill.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">628d1b7a-e010-11f1-9f24-738203d63293</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:03:51 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Abdul Saboor</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France marks 11th anniversary of Paris attacks with tribute at Stade de France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-marks-11th-anniversary-of-paris-attacks-with-tribute-at-stade-de-france</link><description>
France is marking the 11th anniversary of the November 2015 Paris terrorist attacks on Friday, with commemorations honouring the 130 people killed. This year the Stade de France, one of the sites targeted by the attackers, hosts a sporting event on 13 November for the first time since the tragedy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a235f704-df5e-11f1-bb2c-85a37d07b862</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg">AP - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France slams Russian ‘intimidation’ as fresh EU sanctions come into force</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-slams-russian-intimidation-fedorova-as-fresh-eu-sanctions-come-into-force</link><description>
The European Union will approve more ​sanctions against Russia on Monday, the bulk of which were proposed by France, the country's Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad said on Thursday. He also warned that Paris would not be intimidated by Moscow’s decision to ban two French journalists and two MPs from entering the country.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9187c500-de81-11f1-bc9f-6b48e96878ad</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:44:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg">© RFI</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France requests arrest warrants for Iranian suspects over supermarket cyberattack</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-france-requests-arrest-warrants-for-iranian-suspects-over-supermarket-cyberattack</link><description>
France has requested international arrest warrants for three Iranian men over October’s cyberattack on supermarket fridges, while Tehran rejects the allegations as “baseless and malicious”. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8a8f8ab4-ddcb-11f1-8b47-cfca036f86fe</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:00:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race vowing to expel unemployed foreigners</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-zemmour-joins-2027-race-vowing-to-expel-jobless-foreigners</link><description>
Far-right politician Eric Zemmour has formally entered next year’s French presidential race. He is promising a sharp cut in immigration, and the expulsion of foreigners who are out of work, even if they live in France legally.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e4ed6918-ddc6-11f1-ab44-f53e2031ebff</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:55:43 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg">© SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron file new lawsuit in US against right-wing influencer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-emmanuel-and-brigitte-macron-file-new-lawsuit-in-us-against-right-wing-influencer</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte have filed a new defamation lawsuit in the United States against conservative influencer Candace Owens, who claims the French First Lady is a transgender woman.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e1014d56-dcf9-11f1-b466-e9d2e52e2a56</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:59:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters pool via AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teachers divided over compulsory 11 November ceremonies at schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-teachers-divided-over-compulsory-11-november-ceremonies-at-schools</link><description>
A new government initiative requires primary schools across France to hold ceremonies honouring those who died for the country. But teachers are divided over its purpose and the role of the military in education. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8f4305e2-dd0b-11f1-ad88-012109f6bc5c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:05:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG">REUTERS/Pascal Rosssignol</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students demonstrate solidarity in the fight for better schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-students-demonstrate-solidarity-in-the-fight-for-better-schools</link><description>
It began as a protest over crumbling classrooms and missing teachers, but France's student movement is now challenging the political establishment to give young people more of a say in decisions about their future.

Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Unions vow to maintain pressure on government after fourth wave of protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261108-unions-vow-to-keep-pressure-on-french-government-after-fourth-wave-of-protests</link><description>
Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the French government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36cb7bb6-dac6-11f1-b148-e9346ba72bac</guid><pubDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:00:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg">AP Photo/Emma Da Silva - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French students vow to continue protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/video/20261107-french-students-vow-to-continue-protests-paris</link><description>
French pupils and students are protesting and blockading schools over poor conditions and a university admissions system (Parcoursup) seen as over-selective and opaque. Despite recent concessions by the government, students at Hélène Boucher high school in Paris say they'll continue, even after riot place were sent to break their blockade.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c9b5ff0-dab9-11f1-a45a-31b57fcb4ae5</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:02:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261107-france-braces-for-second-day-of-protests-within-48-hours</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33ad1cbc-da96-11f1-8df4-1da1eb33321e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 12:10:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Hannah McKay</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: France's student protests and how they fuelled a larger social movement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261106-podcast-france-s-student-protests-and-how-they-fuelled-a-larger-social-movement-may-68</link><description>
A look at France's high school protests and how they have fed into an ongoing social movement. What are the students protesting against? What impact has the police crackdown had? How has the government reacted? And a comparison with student movements of the past.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bcd965aa-d9cd-11f1-b272-af07f9a85ea6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:29:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-french-lawyers-to-sue-interior-minister-over-mutilation-of-young-protesters</link><description>
Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dba18ef0-d9e5-11f1-863b-f351e1b5079d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:39:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nacho Doce</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-one-quarter-of-young-bullying-victims-turning-to-ai-for-help-study-finds</link><description>
As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71185a8c-d797-11f1-a35f-45b5729425b2</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:35:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg">© pixabay / Yamu_Jay</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-chilling-figures-show-domestic-violence-still-major-problem-in-france</link><description>
French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">77dc943a-d92e-11f1-90a5-5193511bd582</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:08:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg">© Andreea Alexandru / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>‘Jensen Huang lost his mind’: how AI’s smartest man fell for the world’s oldest trick</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/14/jensen-huang-affair-nvidia-nightmare</link>
      <description><p>Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true</p><p>The resignation this week of Nvidia’s founder and CEO Jensen Huang is one of the most astonishing corporate scandals in memory, featuring allegations of international espionage and extramarital affairs involving one of the world’s most powerful men. As investigations mount into what went wrong at the $4tn chip company, the saga may also become a milestone in the decades-long history of spies infiltrating the US tech industry.</p><p>Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife of 41 years in a letter to employees this past weekend, following a <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html">report from the New York Times</a> that the tech mogul had a close relationship with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China’s government. Huang <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">resigned on Thursday</a> after 33 years as CEO amid reports of two additional affairs with Nvidia employees, causing the world’s most valuable chip company’s stock to plummet.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/14/jensen-huang-affair-nvidia-nightmare">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘It’s frustrating’: chaos at US airports as stoppage grinds travel plans to a halt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/us-airports-flight-stoppage</link>
      <description><p>Travelers and crew feeling ‘pissed’ or ‘lucky’ depending on level of upset amid nationwide ground stop</p><p></p><p>The decision to ground all flights on Friday by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) threw airports and travel plans into chaos across the country, as passengers on planes and in airport terminals were suddenly thrust into limbo.</p><p>At New York’s John F Kennedy airport, passengers found their travel plans abruptly canceled – some even after they had boarded their planes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/us-airports-flight-stoppage">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/world">World news</category>
      <pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 02:49:59 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/us-airports-flight-stoppage</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7ed43949a5180577da723e2bf8cbe9c1ff30a73b/116_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=a42d4b21d85e960cc27767128ff75b5b">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPA</media:credit>
      </media:content>
      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7ed43949a5180577da723e2bf8cbe9c1ff30a73b/116_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=2890ba2af4dc8081facb5fdc8b1c5c37">

      <description><p>CEO behind the meteoric rise of Nvidia stepped down after it was revealed he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy </p><p>Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a>, the company at the center of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai">AI</a> boom, after leading it for more than 30 years.</p><p>Huang, an electrical engineer by education, stewarded the company from a $1bn firm when it went public in 1999 to a company valued at more than $4tn in 2026.       <description><p>Rallies are planned at more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks</p><p>Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are planning rallies at <a href="https://starbucksworkersunited.controlshift.app/events?link_id=2&amp;can_id=debd8d2ad19f005d15f9bbdff314d42a&amp;source=email-nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;email_referrer=email_3490793&amp;email_subject=nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;&amp;">over 40 college campuses</a> across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott campaign</a> as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.</p><p>Starbucks Workers United is <a href="https://sbworkersunited.org/what-were-fighting-for-updates-on-contract-bargaining/">seeking</a> better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store.       <description><p>Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high</p><p>US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by high <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/mortgage-rates">mortgage rates</a> and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.</p><p>Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/11/democrats-election-medicaid-costs</link>
      <description><p>‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’</p><p>Is this an opportunity for a new America? As the Reagan revolution four decades ago launched US society down the path to low taxes and meager solidarity, perhaps the Republican bloodbath last week could turn US politics toward building a new social contract anchored on an aspiration to equitable prosperity.</p><p>One can sense the ambition of the bumper new crop of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrats</a> ushered to power last week, calling for support for programs for children and their parents; emphatically endorsing the long-held dream of Medicare for All. The project includes rolling back <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s cuts to Medicaid and food stamps, and restoring subsidies for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act that Republicans allowed to expire.       <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case.       <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. The kitten – so tiny she fit in the palm of Teixeira’s hand – needed to be bottle-fed every few hours. For weeks, Teixeira set her alarm for middle-of-the-night feedings and drove home on her lunch break to care for the kitten she named Milo. As the cat grew, so did the connection between them.</p><p>“We just bonded,” Teixeira says. “Like mother and daughter.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/apr/24/pet-memorial-jewelry-small-business">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year.</p><p>What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. It was the same scoreline and the same feeling for Tuchel on Sunday night.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/terry-butcher-ive-learned-to-live-with-the-hand-of-god-goal-better</link>
      <description><p>The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places</p><p>“Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona.</p><p>Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/terry-butcher-ive-learned-to-live-with-the-hand-of-god-goal-better">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/record-breaking-andy-robertson-is-scotlands-finest-captain</link>
      <description><p>As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart </p><p>Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup.</p><p>There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/record-breaking-andy-robertson-is-scotlands-finest-captain">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/afc-wimbledon-a-failed-87m-investment-bid-and-the-challenge-for-fan-ownership</link>
      <description><p>Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can</p><p>When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium.</p><p>AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/afc-wimbledon-a-failed-87m-investment-bid-and-the-challenge-for-fan-ownership">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league</link>
      <description><p>Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding</p><p>In the final, absurdly tense moments before <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">England finally did it</a> and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: <em>s</em><em>omehow, anyhow</em>. What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too.</p><p>Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Mauricio Pochettino asked the US to believe in his project. Did he believe in it himself?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/mauricio-pochettino-usmnt-legacy-belief</link>
      <description><p>The coach’s tenure with the USMNT brought a whiplash of highs and lows. He met some goals but also left many with the impression he never truly bought in</p><p>It did not take US men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino very long to take his first big swing.</p><p>He’d just taken the reins of the program after a disastrous performance at the 2024 Copa América cost his predecessor his job, with the first home World Cup in three decades looming on the horizon. The federation <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2024/oct/13/mauricio-pochettino-usmnt-debut-soccer-panama">introduced</a> him in New York City, on the 24th floor of a building overlooking the Hudson River. In short order, he was asked about the culture surrounding the program.       <title>Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/kansas-city-current-gotham-fc-nwsl-semi-final-haley-hopkins</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset</p></li><li><p>Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds</p></li><li><p>Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title</p></li></ul><p>After a week dominated by a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/washington-spirit-semifinal-audi-field-gotham-nwsl-playoffs">headline-grabbing stadium imbroglio</a>, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital business of their NWSL semi-final on Sunday afternoon, a frigid encounter at an unlikely venue on New York City’s Randall’s Island with a place in next Saturday’s championship match at stake.</p><p>Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley <a href="https://x.com/NWSL/status/2122090637860434332">off the crossbar and in</a> to seal a 2-1 upset that left Gotham FC’s title defense in tatters. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the defending champions into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/kansas-city-current-gotham-fc-nwsl-semi-final-haley-hopkins">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Raphinha sees red as Brazil stunned by Japan while Argentina’s post-Messi era starts with defeat</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/brazil-argentina-japan-uruguay-wales-norway-portugal-denmark</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Brazil loss in Singapore marred by unruly end to friendly</p></li><li><p>Argentina beaten 2-1 by Uruguay in Buenos Aires</p></li></ul><p>Raphinha was sent off as <strong>Brazil</strong> crashed to a 3-2 defeat by <strong>Japan</strong> in their international friendly in Singapore. The Barcelona captain had been substituted after 71 minutes, but was shown a red card after protesting against Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time winner on the touchline. The Brazil head coach, Carlo Ancelotti, was also sent off in a fractious ending to the match.</p><p>Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinícius Júnior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/brazil-argentina-japan-uruguay-wales-norway-portugal-denmark">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/washington-spirit-utah-royals-nwsl-semi-final-clara-luvanga</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Tanzanian scores second-half winner in 2-1 victory</p></li><li><p>Spirit reach fifth NWSL final and third in succession</p></li><li><p>Washington will chase second title at home ground</p></li></ul><p>Clara Luvanga scored her second goal of the postseason in the 57th minute, capitalizing on an errant pass as the Washington Spirit reached their fifth NWSL Championship and third straight with a 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals on Saturday.</p><p>Luvanga raced on to Nuria Rábano’s ill-advised ball after it rolled past Utah center-back Tatumn Milazzo, then chipped it delicately over the advancing goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn for the winner.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/washington-spirit-utah-royals-nwsl-semi-final-clara-luvanga">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/fifa-kozo-tashima-seeks-change-of-tone</link>
      <description><p>Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football</p><p>Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino.</p><p>The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/japan-fa-head-kozo-tashima-stand-against-gianni-infantino-for-fifa-president">an unlikely challenger</a> to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/fifa-kozo-tashima-seeks-change-of-tone">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Manager calls Sunday’s Nations League decider a ‘final’ as preparations for Euro 2028 ratchet up a level</p><p>Proof of concept. It is Thomas Tuchel’s latest buzz phrase. The England manager has dropped it into the conversation pretty regularly since the Friday of last week when he named his squad for this international window, the one that was always going to decide whether his team finished first or second in their Nations League group.</p><p>By it, Tuchel means a test of his methods, what he is trying to build – or, more accurately, fine-tune – as he turns his gaze towards Euro 2028 and tries to move on from the devastation of the World Cup <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/15/england-argentina-world-cup-semi-final-match-report">semi-final exit against Argentina</a>.       <title>Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/portugal-cristiano-ronaldo-football-memories-future</link>
      <description><p>The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years </p><p>There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/cristiano-ronaldo-calls-time-on-portugal-career">their first game without him</a>.</p><p>The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/portugal-cristiano-ronaldo-football-memories-future">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/pochettino-chelsea-maelstrom-yardstick-what-lies-ahead-manchester-united</link>
      <description><p>Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team</p><p>Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/02/premier-league-managers-arteta-alonso-de-zerbi-carrick-klopp-guardiola">big beasts</a>” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.</p><p>Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jun/01/tottenham-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report">2019 Champions League final</a>. His presence lifted those clubs.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/pochettino-chelsea-maelstrom-yardstick-what-lies-ahead-manchester-united">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players</p><p>Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to <a href="https://www.instagram.com/p/DRVlP5iEgRR/?img_index=2">run at 81% of her max speed</a> at 32 weeks pregnant.</p><p>Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/angel-city-fc">Angel City FC</a>, documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. <rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title><![CDATA[France 24 - Infos, news & actualités - L'information internationale en direct]]></title><description>France 24 décrypte l’actualité internationale, politique, l’économie, l’environnement, la culture, le sport, en France et à l’international avec analyses, des interviews, des reportages exclusifs, des magazines et des documentaires.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 02:47:11 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Les Tchèques manifestent massivement contre la réforme du financement des médias publics</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/europe/20261116-tcheques-manifestent-en-masse-contre-reforme-financement-medias-publics-redevance-andrej-babis-liberte-presse</link><description>
Des centaines de milliers de Tchèques se sont rassemblés dimanche à Prague contre le projet du gouvernement visant à réduire la redevance des médias publics et à transférer les fonds vers le budget de l'État. L'initiative du gouvernement d'Andrej Babis est dénoncée par ses opposants comme une menace pour la liberté de la presse.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b90c524-e165-11f1-8bad-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-15T160533Z-1645454597-RC2FOOA3ZEB0-RTRMADP-3-CZECH-MEDIA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b90c524-e165-11f1-8bad-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-15T160533Z-1645454597-RC2FOOA3ZEB0-RTRMADP-3-CZECH-MEDIA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">982f1e96-e163-11f1-a9f8-d3145b9c4877</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 02:34:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9b90c524-e165-11f1-8bad-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-15T160533Z-1645454597-RC2FOOA3ZEB0-RTRMADP-3-CZECH-MEDIA.jpg">© Eva Korinkova, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Réforme du financement des médias publics : les Tchèques manifestent en masse</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-r%C3%A9forme-du-financement-des-m%C3%A9dias-publics-les-tch%C3%A8ques-manifestent-en-masse</link><description>
Des manifestants à perte de vue au parc Letna de Prague. Ce lieu de contestation historique de la capitale tchèque accueille, dimanche, son plus grand rassemblement depuis la Révolution de velours en 1989. Le motif : la défense de l'audiovisuel public. L'exécutif souhaite remplacer l'actuel système de redevance finançant la télévision et la radio publiques tchèques par un financement assuré directement par le budget de l'État.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/66446a36-e162-11f1-ac14-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-020902-021039-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/66446a36-e162-11f1-ac14-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-020902-021039-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6b97c866-e162-11f1-b694-13c1f41a9c06</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 02:09:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Aden, au Yémen, se barricade face à l'offensive des Houthis</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261116-aden-au-y%C3%A9men-se-barricade-face-%C3%A0-l-offensive-des-houthis</link><description>
Les rebelles Houthis revendiquent la prise de zones montagneuses, tout près du détroit stratégique de Bab el-Mandeb. Ils se trouvent à quelques dizaines de kilomètres de la ville d'Aden, faisant réagir les forces yéménites. Le camp gouvernemental redéploie des troupes dans le sud du pays, selon des sources militaires et gouvernementales dimanche à l'AFP. Des attaques houthies avaient déjà visé ces dernières semaines le palais présidentiel à Aden et l'aéroport de la ville.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33c58212-e161-11f1-b542-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-020148-020333-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33c58212-e161-11f1-b542-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261116-020148-020333-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">391b06ec-e161-11f1-8666-c30ec3a145c7</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 02:06:20 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Éco/Tech</category><title>Elon Musk et plus de 157 000 signataires réclament le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9co-tech/20261116-elon-musk-uber-spacex-epic-games-157000-signataires-reclament-retour-jensen-huang-tete-nvidia-intelligence-artificielle-lettre-ouverte-enquete-independante</link><description>
Plusieurs patrons de la Silicon Valley, dont Elon Musk et Tim Sweeney, font partie des 157 000 signataires d'une lettre ouverte qui demande le retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de Nvidia, "pendant qu'une enquête indépendante établit les faits". Selon eux, il "mérite une procédure équitable, pas un tribunal populaire".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a400e0-c867-11f1-a40c-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-08T175236Z-1478285321-RC25ZNARJMDM-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a400e0-c867-11f1-a40c-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-08T175236Z-1478285321-RC25ZNARJMDM-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99c5ba0c-e150-11f1-8130-5f504f401ddf</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 00:11:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20a400e0-c867-11f1-a40c-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-08T175236Z-1478285321-RC25ZNARJMDM-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP.jpg">© Evan Vucci, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Alpinisme : l'expédition du Jannu Est, "un tournant" pour Benjamin Védrines</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261115-alpinisme-l-exp%C3%A9dition-du-jannu-est-un-tournant-pour-benjamin-v%C3%A9drines</link><description>
Après huit mois loin de la scène médiatique, l'alpiniste Benjamin Védrines fait son retour en cette fin 2026. Au côtés d'un autre alpinistre français Nicolas Jean, il vient de remporter le Piolet d'Or, l'une des plus hautes distinction de l'alpinisme. Ce trophée vient récompenser leur ascension du Jannu Est (7 468 m) au Népal, une première dans l'histoire après de nombreux échecs au cours des dernières décennies.

Publié dimanche, un arrêté préfectoral prévoit l'interdiction de tout rassemblement ou cortège non déclaré "dans un rayon de 100 mètres" autour de dix lycées et cinq sites universitaires de Paris. La mesure, qui s'applique de lundi à vendredi inclus, est justifiée par "les nombreux débordements et blocages", assure le préfet de police Patrice Faure.

Le candidat tout juste déclaré Teddy Riner est crédité de 4,5 % des intentions de vote dans un sondage pour BFMTV et La Tribune Dimanche. Selon cette enquête, le maire de Cannes, David Lisnard, fait un bon de quatre points au détriment de Bruno Retailleau. Marine Le Pen reste en tête des intentions de vote, suivie par Jean-Luc Mélenchon, qui s'installe à la deuxième place. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">480c5ff2-e0d5-11f1-b132-ad05df6f53f9</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:35:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/af92d8aa-e0d4-11f1-a352-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C6WN7K6.jpg">© Valery Hache, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Acte V du mouvement social : des revendications variées, une affluence en baisse</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-acte-v-du-mouvement-social-des-revendications-vari%C3%A9es-une-affluence-en-baisse</link><description>
Lors de l'acte V du mouvement social qui ébranle la France, quelque 106 000 à 200 000 personnes ont défilé samedi dans toute la France, selon les chiffres du ministère de l'Intérieur et l'intersyndicale jeune (Union étudiane, USL, Fage, Unef). Quelques incidents se sont produits et des journalistes ont été agressés.

Maileva, filiale du groupe La Poste, a été victime d'une cyberattaque mi-septembre ayant conduit au vol des coordonnées de 22 millions de personnes. L'an dernier, une cyberattaque revendiquée par des hackers prorusses avait déjà touché La Poste à quelques jours de Noël.
